# Investment Screening Memo: Stripe

**Website:** https://stripe.com · **As of:** 2026-11-04

> Programmable financial infrastructure for internet businesses: payments, billing, tax and treasury APIs, now extending into stablecoins and agentic commerce.

*Screening memo generated by an AI research agent from public sources. Not investment advice. Verify every figure before relying on it.*

## 1. Company Snapshot

| | |
|---|---|
| **What they do** | API-first payments platform that also sells a Revenue suite (Billing, Invoicing, Tax, etc.) and stablecoin infrastructure through Bridge and Privy. [[1]](https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-2025-update)[[11]](https://blockworks.co/news/stripe-acquires-privy-wallet)[[12]](https://www.fintechfutures.com/m-a/stripe-continues-crypto-push-with-privy-acquisition) |
| **Business model** | Mostly usage-based fees on payment volume plus software fees; the Revenue suite was said to be on track for a ~$1B annual run rate (2025 letter, Feb 2026). Net revenue is not publicly disclosed; Sacra estimates ~$6.9B for 2025. [[1]](https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-2025-update)[[8]](https://sacra.com/research/stripe) |
| **Customers** | Says it powers more than 5 million businesses directly or via platforms, including the top AI companies (2025 letter, Feb 2026). [[1]](https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-2025-update) |
| **Stage** | Late-stage private and profitable (company-stated for 2025); valued at $159B in a Feb 2026 employee tender offer, with management saying there is no rush to IPO (Jan 2026). [[1]](https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-2025-update)[[2]](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-02-24/stripe-hits-159-billion-valuation-as-payment-volume-soars)[[7]](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-01-20/stripe-s-collison-says-no-rush-for-payment-firm-to-go-public) |
| **Funding** | Last primary round: $6.5B Series I at a $50B valuation (Mar 2023), bringing total raised to about $8.7B; since then, secondary tender offers (most recently $159B, Feb 2026, led by Thrive, Coatue and a16z). [[4]](https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2023/03/203780-fintech-stripe-raises-6-5-billion-at-50-billion-valuation-a-big-drop-from-prior-round/)[[5]](https://nairametrics.com/2023/03/16/stripe-raises-6-5-billion-in-series-i-funding-to-hit-50-billion-valuation/)[[3]](https://www.theblock.co/post/391075/stripe-valuation-jumps-to-159-billion-on-back-of-tender-offer) |
| **Location** | Dual-headquartered in South San Francisco, California and Dublin, Ireland; founded in 2010 by Patrick and John Collison. [[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stripe,_Inc.) |

## 2. Market and Competition

- McKinsey (Sep 2025) estimates global payments revenue at ~$2.5T on ~$2.0 quadrillion of value flows, growing ~4%/yr after a slowdown in 2024. [[13]](https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/financial-services/our-insights/global-payments-report)
- Stripe's 2025 TPV was ~$1.9T, up 34% YoY, or about 1.6% of global GDP, so it is still taking share in a slow-growing pool. [[1]](https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-2025-update)
- Stablecoin payment volume roughly doubled to ~$400B in 2025, an estimated 60% of it B2B, which opens a new rail Stripe is building into. [[1]](https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-2025-update)
- Agentic commerce is emerging: Stripe co-developed the Agentic Commerce Protocol with OpenAI and powers Instant Checkout in ChatGPT (Sep 2025). [[9]](https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-openai-instant-checkout)

**Key competitors**

- **Adyen**: Public, enterprise-focused rival; FY2025 processed volume ~EUR 1.39T and net revenue ~EUR 2.36B, growing more slowly than Stripe. [[21]](https://www.itiger.com/hant/news/1131997847)
- **PayPal (Braintree)**: Incumbent with ~$1.79T 2025 TPV; Braintree unbranded processing gave up volume in H1 2025 to focus on profitable growth. [[20]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633917/000163391726000024/pypl-20251231.htm)[[22]](https://www.panabee.com/news/paypal-earnings-2025-annual)
- **Checkout.com**: Enterprise and platform challenger: $12B internal valuation (Sep 2025) and $300B+ processed in 2025, up 64% YoY. [[18]](https://www.checkout.com/newsroom/checkout-com-accelerates-towards-full-year-profitability-and-announces-employee-share-buy-back-and-a-new-12bn-valuation)[[19]](https://www.checkout.com/guides-and-reports/annual-letter-2025)

## 3. Investment Thesis

- Scale and growth together: TPV grew from ~$1.4T (2024) to ~$1.9T (2025), with the company profitable. [[23]](https://ffnews.com/blog/2025/02/28/stripes-total-payment-volume-reaches-1-4t-as-long-standing-investments-in-ai-pay-off)[[1]](https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-2025-update)
- Expanding beyond payments: a ~$1B run-rate Revenue suite raises take rate and switching costs beyond processing alone. [[1]](https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-2025-update)
- Early position in stablecoin rails, built from the $1.1B Bridge acquisition, Privy wallets, the Tempo L1 (mainnet Mar 2026) and a conditionally approved OCC trust charter (Feb 2026). [[12]](https://www.fintechfutures.com/m-a/stripe-continues-crypto-push-with-privy-acquisition)[[11]](https://blockworks.co/news/stripe-acquires-privy-wallet)[[10]](https://www.bankless.com/read/news/stripe-deploys-tempo-blockchain-to-mainnet-introduces-machine-payments-protocol.md)[[15]](https://cointelegraph.com/news/bridge-stripe-occ-approval-national-trust-bank)
- Default processor for the AI wave: it serves top AI companies and co-authored the Agentic Commerce Protocol with OpenAI. [[1]](https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-2025-update)[[9]](https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-openai-instant-checkout)

## 4. Risks and Red Flags

- Opaque financials: net revenue, take rate and margins are undisclosed, and third-party estimates (e.g. Sacra) are the only revenue figures. [[8]](https://sacra.com/research/stripe)
- Valuation: $159B (Feb 2026) is ~3x the $50B Series I mark and ~74% above the prior year's tender, leaving little room for a growth slowdown. [[2]](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-02-24/stripe-hits-159-billion-valuation-as-payment-volume-soars)[[3]](https://www.theblock.co/post/391075/stripe-valuation-jumps-to-159-billion-on-back-of-tender-offer)[[4]](https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2023/03/203780-fintech-stripe-raises-6-5-billion-at-50-billion-valuation-a-big-drop-from-prior-round/)
- Take-rate pressure: McKinsey flags agentic and autonomous payments as a threat to card fee revenue, and Adyen and Checkout.com compete hard for enterprise volume. [[13]](https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/financial-services/our-insights/global-payments-report)[[18]](https://www.checkout.com/newsroom/checkout-com-accelerates-towards-full-year-profitability-and-announces-employee-share-buy-back-and-a-new-12bn-valuation)
- Regulatory and crypto exposure: the bank lobby group ICBA opposed Bridge's national trust charter, and stablecoin businesses add compliance and reputational risk. [[16]](https://www.icba.org/w/icba-urges-occ-to-reject-stripe-s-national-trust-bank-charter-application)[[14]](https://www.occ.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/public-comment/bridge-national-trust-bank.pdf)
- Red flag (minor): a 300-role (~3.5%) cut in Jan 2025, even though the company planned to keep growing headcount. [[17]](https://www.bankingdive.com/news/stripe-cuts-300-employees/737977/)

## 5. Potential Acquirers and Strategic Investors

- **IPO / public markets**: The most plausible exit at this size, though the Collisons say there is no rush to list (Jan 2026). [[7]](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-01-20/stripe-s-collison-says-no-rush-for-payment-firm-to-go-public)
- **Thrive Capital, Coatue, a16z**: Main buyers in the Feb 2026 tender, likely to keep providing private liquidity. [[3]](https://www.theblock.co/post/391075/stripe-valuation-jumps-to-159-billion-on-back-of-tender-offer)
- **GIC / Temasek (sovereign funds)**: Joined the 2023 Series I; natural buyers of large pre-IPO secondary blocks. [[4]](https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2023/03/203780-fintech-stripe-raises-6-5-billion-at-50-billion-valuation-a-big-drop-from-prior-round/)
- **Visa or Mastercard**: Analytical: a strategic stake or partnership in network-adjacent rails (stablecoins, agentic tokens); a full acquisition is unlikely given size and antitrust.

## 6. Open Questions for Management

1. What were 2025 net revenue, take rate and non-GAAP operating margin, and how did they split between payments and the Revenue suite?
2. How concentrated is TPV among the top 20 customers and platforms, and what is net revenue retention by segment?
3. How much revenue do stablecoins (Bridge, Tempo) bring in today, and what is the path to material contribution?
4. How does take rate on AI-company and agentic (ACP) volume compare with traditional e-commerce?
5. What is the status of Bridge's OCC charter after the Feb 2026 conditional approval, and which capabilities depend on it?
6. What would trigger an IPO decision, and how often will tender offers continue?
7. Where is Stripe losing enterprise deals to Adyen or Checkout.com, and on what criteria?
